lesson.title: They Cross. You Cover.
lesson.hook: You serve. Your partner moves across the net as the receiver meets the ball.
lesson.liveIntro: You serve. Your partner moves across the net as the receiver meets the ball.

dcA.name: What does this next ball call for?
dcA.sit: Their reply comes back to your pair. Watch where it reaches your racket.
dcA.q: What does this next ball call for?
opts: Use controlled depth through the middle

lines.A: You give the ball room and prepare together for another reply.
lines.B: It lands here, but the smaller target leaves less margin. Keep covering.

dcA.take: Partner crosses. Cover the space they leave.
dcA.payoff: Partner crosses. Cover the space they leave.
dcA.principle: Partner crosses. Cover the space they leave.
dcA.why: A crossing net partner changes the server’s coverage job. Move while the ball travels, then read the actual reply. The cover is an adjustment to this crossing movement, not an automatic switch after every serve.

dc.name: Your partner is crossing. Where do you move?
dc.sit: You serve. Your partner moves across the net as the receiver meets the ball.
dc.q: Your partner is crossing. Where do you move?

lines.A: You cover behind your crossing partner. Both halves have an owner.
lines.B: You stay on the same half as your partner. The reply sends you across late.

pro.label: The Bryans · A few words before the serve
pro.moment: The Bryan brothers made their teamwork look instinctive. Asked how they planned points, they described quick signals and short code words: “we don’t need a long conversation”. Knowing the intended serve gave the net player an early picture of the return.
pro.read: Your next point: agree the serve and the move. When your partner crosses, cover the space they leave. A few words beforehand can prevent two players doing the same job.
pro.src: Bob & Mike Bryan · Interview with Mark Hodgkinson · Tennisplayer

drill.name: Rehearse as a pair
drill.how: Agree a serve target and a crossing signal. Play the return and two more balls. After each point, both name the space they were covering.
